mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in initial jobless claims (UNRATE proxy via labor market softening) signals weakening household demand, which reduces earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND UNRATE > previous month by >0.2pp
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when GDP growth is simultaneously recovering.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of at least 50,000 for three consecutive months, accompanied by stable unemployment (UNRATE flat), signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month by >50,000 for 3 consecutive months AND UNRATE change within ±0.1pp
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during such episodes, or the effect reverses when wage growth accelerates sharply.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for two consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month by >0.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such periods, or the effect is absent during supply-chain normalization.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1.2 million units for three consecutive months signals weakening residential investment, which negatively impacts construction and related sectors and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods, or the effect is reversed during a sharp rebound in housing demand.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.75 percentage points signals an aggressive tightening stance, which immediately raises risk-free rates and equity discount rates, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative after such a rate hike, or the effect is absent during periods of strong earnings surprises.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a fall in payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 30,000 in the same month signals a significant labor market deterioration, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > previous month by >0.2pp AND PAYEMS < previous month by >30,000
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such joint signals, or the effect is reversed during rapid policy easing.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annual increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 4% for four consecutive months signals entrenched inflation, which increases the probability of sustained restrictive monetary policy and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL YoY change > 4% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such periods, or the effect is absent when inflation expectations stabilize.
